intro: Active SharePoint exploits are dropping ransomware and knocking out EDR. Patch key apps, review Mac privacy changes, and tighten Unix privilege tools before tickets start flying.

items.heading: SharePoint exploits disable EDR, drop ransomware
items.body: Attackers are exploiting SharePoint to kill security tooling and launch ransomware. If SharePoint is exposed or behind on cumulative updates, you are on borrowed time. Patch to current CUs, pull SharePoint off the public internet where possible, and sweep for webshells and EDR tamper events.

items.heading: Warlock targets utilities via SharePoint flaws
items.body: The Warlock gang is abusing SharePoint bugs to breach utilities, telecoms, and government orgs in Portuguese and Spanish speaking regions. This is not theoretical, it is a live campaign. Lock down external access, apply the latest SharePoint updates, and increase monitoring on internet facing portals.

items.heading: Fortra BoKS critical auth bypass and RCE
items.body: Serious flaws in Fortra BoKS allow authentication bypass, remote command execution, and memory corruption on managed Unix hosts, putting privileged access controls at risk. Treat this like a domain controller level emergency for Unix estates. Patch immediately, audit BoKS activity, and rotate credentials for accounts managed by or stored in BoKS.

items.heading: GitLab AI Gateway RCE on self-hosted
items.body: A logged in Duo Agent Platform user could execute arbitrary commands on self hosted GitLab AI Gateway. Fixes are available in 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1. Update now and restrict access to the gateway until patched.

items.heading: macOS Full Disk Access gets tighter
items.body: Apple is tightening Full Disk Access to stop AI agents and other apps from quietly reading messages and files. Mac admins should expect behavior changes in FDA bound apps. Review MDM profiles, re approve required apps, and test automation that relies on FDA before users do.

items.heading: Frontline Education breach hits K 12 staff
items.body: Attackers exploited a third party flaw to steal employee data, including Social Security numbers, from Frontline Education. If you support K 12 districts using Frontline, assume staff PII may be impacted. Coordinate with districts on notifications, offer identity protection, and watch for payroll or tax fraud signals.

items.heading: Ransomware knocks Vicksburg city systems
items.body: Vicksburg shut down systems after a ransomware hit, and the FBI is investigating. Municipal environments remain soft targets. Use this as a tabletop prompt, validate offline backups, segment critical services, and rehearse your isolation and restore steps.

items.heading: YARA X 1.21.0 speeds up rule scanning
items.body: YARA X 1.21.0 delivers five improvements and four bug fixes that stabilize and speed rule scanning across DFIR and detection workflows. Upgrade in your analysis stacks to cut scan time and reduce flakiness. Run regression tests on your rule packs after the bump.

title: Zero day heat, SharePoint hits, and AI-driven mischief
intro: Patch queues are full and bots are busy. Prioritize the mail gateway, SharePoint, and identity guardrails before coffee cools.

items.heading: FortiMail zero day exploited
items.body: Fortinet says CVE-2026-104286 is being abused in the wild. If you run FortiMail, apply the vendor’s workaround now, lock down exposure, and line up maintenance windows for patches as soon as they drop. Watch for unusual admin actions and config changes on the gateway.

items.heading: Warlock hits unpatched SharePoint
items.body: A Warlock group is going after vulnerable SharePoint servers. Patch fast, restrict external access, and sweep for webshells plus odd IIS patterns that suggest post-exploit persistence. If you cannot patch today, consider isolating or geofencing access until you can.

items.heading: AI agents fling SQLi at gov sites
items.body: Automated tools launched SQL injection attempts at US and Canadian government sites, a sign that bots are scaling classic web vulns. Lock down apps with parameterized queries and strict input validation, tune WAF rules for SQLi signatures, and monitor for botty traffic spikes. Treat any unauthenticated query errors as a hunting signal.

items.heading: AI agents keep access after tasks
items.body: Identity teams report AI agents holding long-lived permissions and taking actions on users’ behalf. Enforce least privilege and time-bound access, log all agent activity, and bring them under your PAM controls. Treat agents like service accounts with tight scopes and revocation on task completion.

items.heading: Insiders for sale
items.body: Crews are paying employees to reset accounts and tweak transactions. Tighten least privilege and approval workflows, monitor for anomalous employee activity, and keep ethics hotlines front and center. Rotate duties where you can and flag risky access changes for review.

items.heading: Microsoft X account hijacked for token scam
items.body: Attackers briefly hijacked Microsoft’s X account to push a crypto token to 13 million followers. Lock down social accounts with phishing-resistant MFA and strong credential hygiene, and remove shared logins. Review access to any social media tooling and audit for stale tokens.

items.heading: Android 17 locks accessibility abuse
items.body: Android 17 will limit accessibility APIs to verified apps, a big clampdown on malware abusing those services. If you manage Android fleets, enable Advanced Protection and audit app permissions and MDM policies ahead of rollout. Expect fewer fake overlay attacks if you enforce these controls.

items.heading: Android 17 adds forensic logging
items.body: Google is adding off-device forensic logs to help expose spyware and similar stalkware. Update eligible devices, and make sure your mobile EDR and incident response playbooks can collect and analyze those logs. This should speed up investigations and raise the bar for stealthy surveillance apps.

signOff: Back to tickets, but keep one eye on those patch windows.

title: Zero-days, leaked creds, and remote helpdesk RCEs
intro: Active exploits on core tools and some policy shifts to mind. Patch priority first, then go hunt for creds and persistence.

items.heading: Cisco SD-WAN Manager zero-day is live
items.body: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-76504 to get unauthenticated admin access on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, and CISA put it on the KEV list. If you run it, patch immediately and assume exposure if you cannot patch today. Check authentication logs and admin actions, and isolate or rebuild any manager showing suspicious changes.

items.heading: Zimbra exploited via crafted emails
items.body: A Zimbra bug, CVE-2026-73570, was exploited before disclosure using crafted emails that need no user interaction under certain configurations. Patch or apply mitigations now to close the hole. Review mail server logs and quarantine queues for unusual or malformed messages targeting Zimbra.

items.heading: Zammad helpdesk zero-days to RCE
items.body: Attackers chained zero-days in Zammad to hijack sessions, achieve remote code execution and root, then escalate privileges. Update Zammad now and verify your instance for unexpected admin actions or new users. Audit server integrity and rotate tokens or credentials used by the app.

items.heading: ScreenConnect client abused for persistence
items.body: Threat actors are dropping the ScreenConnect client on compromised hosts to stick around. Lock down software install rights, block unauthorized ScreenConnect deployments, and monitor for unexpected ScreenConnect services and outbound connections. Rotate admin credentials if you find any surprise installs.

items.heading: Apple PDF crash PoC is public
items.body: A public PoC for CVE-2026-86950 in CoreGraphics can crash iOS and macOS via malicious PDFs, with hints at possible WhatsApp delivery. Install the latest Apple updates across fleet devices. Until patched, caution users on unsolicited PDFs and consider tightening attachment handling in mail and messaging.

items.heading: Half a million live creds on GitHub
items.body: Researchers found 500,000 active credentials exposed on GitHub despite default push protections. Audit your repos for secrets, enable secret scanning, and enforce pre-commit hooks. Rotate any exposed tokens or keys immediately and review CI logs for misuse.

items.heading: Windows 11 flips on settings backup by default
items.body: Windows 11 will enable settings backup by default on Entra-joined systems after 26H2. Before rollout, audit backup policies, data residency, and privacy implications. Set explicit policy controls and inform tenants to avoid surprises.

items.heading: Google gives vetted defenders Gemini 4 Argon
items.body: Google is providing vetted defenders access to Gemini 4 Argon with fewer guardrails and says it already helped find a critical hospital software bug. Expect clients to ask about it and keep your AI usage policies ready. Validate outputs and stick to safe, auditable use cases.

signOff: Patch early, log often, and get back to the queue.

If these appliances face the internet, treat this as incident response until proven otherwise.

items.heading: TeamViewer client and host need urgent patches
items.body: High severity bugs in TeamViewer client and host builds could allow remote code execution and session compromise. Push the latest updates to every endpoint and server, then restart services to ensure the new binaries load. Review remote session logs for anomalies and block outdated versions in your tools.

items.heading: Chrome and Firefox ship fixes for 100+ bugs
items.body: Current Chrome and Firefox releases patch dozens of issues, including code execution and sandbox escape risks via malicious sites. Roll out the updates across your fleet and enforce restarts for active browsers. Prioritize high risk users like admins and anyone who lives in a browser all day.

items.heading: OpenSSL and wolfSSL patch DTLS flaws
items.body: High severity DTLS issues can leak heap memory or crash services, and fixes are shipping for OpenSSL and wolfSSL. Update libraries in servers, containers, and appliances, then redeploy dependent services. Inventory appliances that bundle these stacks and pull vendor updates as they appear.

items.heading: M365 session theft leads to RMM install
items.body: A US focused phishing campaign is hijacking Microsoft 365 sessions, then installing remote management tools to expand access and fraud. Enforce phishing resistant MFA, monitor for token theft, and block unsanctioned RMMs. Tighten conditional access and alert on unusual sign ins and new device enrollments.

items.heading: Nordix Artifactory breach, stop using artifacts
items.body: OpenInfra Europe’s Artifactory at artifactory.nordix.org was compromised. If you pulled anything between August 28 and September 15, quarantine those systems, replace packages from trusted sources, and verify build integrity. Treat affected builds as tainted until you can rebuild clean.

items.heading: AI dev agents posted 13k internal screenshots
items.body: Researchers saw AI coding agents auto posting internal UI images and billing data to public GitHub repos across hundreds of organizations. Audit AI assisted developer workflows and CI bots, restrict tokens and outbound publishing, and disable screenshot or telemetry uploads. Add DLP checks to repos and rotate any exposed credentials.

items.heading: Monitor Claude Enterprise via DLP and SIEM
items.body: Claude Enterprise now exposes a Compliance API so security tools can scan prompts, uploads, and outputs for sensitive data and policy violations. Turn it on and wire it into your DLP and SIEM to keep AI use inside guardrails. Use this to baseline usage and flag data exfil risks before they become incidents.
